# CAR-T Cell Therapy in Rare Pediatric Leukemia

## Background
CAR-T cell therapies have revolutionized treatment of relapsed/refractory B-cell ALL in children.
Tisagenlecleucel achieves 81% complete remission in pediatric ALL.

## Mechanism of Action
Autologous T cells are engineered ex vivo to express a chimeric antigen receptor targeting CD19.
After lymphodepleting chemotherapy, expanded CAR-T cells engraft and eliminate CD19+ malignant cells.

## Biomarkers
Pre-infusion tumor burden, lymphodepletion regimen choice, and CAR-T cell expansion kinetics
predict durable response. CD19 antigen loss is the dominant acquired-resistance mechanism.

## Trials in Progress
ELIANA-2 long-term follow-up demonstrates 5-year OS of 55%. New constructs targeting CD22
and dual CD19/CD22 are under investigation in CITRUS and AMELIA trials.

## Safety Signals
Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurs in 77-93% of patients, severe in 22-46%.
Neurotoxicity (ICANS) rates of 40%. Tocilizumab and steroid management protocols are standard.

## Conclusions
Manufacturing time and access remain barriers. Allogeneic off-the-shelf CAR products
in trial may eventually replace autologous approaches.
